text:
Alex: heads-up — I prototyped an SLO-driven throttle where every org gets a dynamic RPM that tracks recent SLO burn (p95 latency + error budget).
Maria: can you share the high-level design? how does that play with concurrency caps?
Alex: short: two levers — RPM/TPM shaped by recent SLO burn, plus a hard concurrency cap per-org. RPM is soft (gateway), concurrency is enforced at runtime.
Kai: soft RPM in gateway sounds cheap for early rejects. runtime concurrency is more precise but needs cross-pod coordination. tradeoffs spelled out?
Alex: yup. gateway-level limiter reduces wasted work. runtime cap lets us protect shared GPU pools and KV caches. downside: stricter runtime enforcement can cause request queueing/backpressure.
Anna (devex): console UX question — customers need a single panel showing: current RPM, burst credits, concurrency usage, SLO headroom, and an action button for temporary overrides. simple graph + single-number summary.
Samir: telemetry needs: per-org/per-route token_rate, rejected_soft, rejected_hard, fallback_count, latency_buckets (p50/p95/p99), and a SLO_burn gauge. also tag by client_type (interactive/service).
ratebot: Alert: org=acme-prod exceeded soft-RPM by 3x; auto-fallback to model-lite applied (policy id: pf-23a).
Maria: auto-fallbacks are good. can we prefer model-variant fallback over hard reject for paid orgs and critical routes?
Kai: we should codify priority graph: (1) dedicated capacity, (2) paid fallback model variants, (3) burst credits, (4) soft rejects, (5) hard rejects. makes deterministic routing for outages.
Alex: burst credits idea: each org gets a monthly burst pool + ephemeral windowed bucket. refill policy: monthly quota + sliding-window token-bucket for short bursts.
Anna (devex): config UX must expose: baseline RPM per tier, SLO multiplier cap (e.g., up to 2x), concurrency cap, burst budget, and override TTL. default presets for self-serve.
Samir: implementation note: emit a changefeed for policy decisions so we can replay why a request was rejected/served/fallbacked. that'll help eval regressions.
Maria: background jobs problem: service accounts doing batch ingest can blow RPM but should use queued ingest path. we need detection + route classification.
Alex: proposal for enforcement split: gateway enforces soft RPM and emits reason_code; runtime verifies concurrency and enforces final hard rejects. Instrument: reason_code, policy_version, model_variant, fallback_applied.
Kai: sample token-bucket config (gateway):
```
{
  "baseline_rpm": 1200,
  "slo_multiplier_max": 2.0,
  "burst_window_secs": 60,
  "burst_tokens": 600
}
```
Maria: question: how do we surface simulated impact before rolling policy? need a preview/sim tool in console that replays X minutes of trace under new policy.
Anna (devex): I'll build a mockup for preview simulator + admin rollback flow. include TTL for manual overrides and audit trail.
Samir: metrics schema TODO: add "policy_evaluations_total" with labels {org,route,outcome,reason}. also add histogram for queue_time before runtime cap.
Alex: next steps: I'll write RFC with flow diagrams and policy state machine. short-term milestone: implement gateway soft-RPM + telemetry; follow-up: runtime concurrency enforcement.
Anna (devex): I'll prepare console mockups and a UX for policy presets.
Kai: I'll own runtime enforcement spikes + cross-pod coordination design.
Maria: I'll enumerate edge cases & SLA tier mapping (free/dev/starter/prod).
Alex: ETA for RFC + prototype? aim EOW.
Anna (devex): noted, will sync once RFC is up. :thumbsup:
